title: Beijing's Drum Tower Still Drums - 24 Drums, One Left | China Travel Expert
description:
Beijing's Drum Tower still beats a drum - and it once kept time for the whole city.

The Drum Tower (Gulou) stands on Beijing's old central axis, paired with the Bell Tower just to the north. For centuries its drums marked the night watches: it held a large night-watch drum plus 24 smaller drums for the 24 solar terms (25 in all), of which only one Qing-dynasty original survives today. The current tower dates mainly to the Ming and Qing after fires and rebuilds. Visitors can still catch a short drum performance staged through the day, played on replica drums.

🧭 Expert Tip: Performance times shift by season (recent trials even extended weekend hours), so check the posted schedule when you arrive - then walk two minutes north to the Bell Tower and into the surrounding hutongs.
